chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the bequest, and he said: 'It is a right upon every Muslim.'

key_terms.الوصية: The bequest/will (wasiyya) — a legal disposition of property or instructions to be carried out after death; a recognized obligation in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.حق: Right/obligation (haqq) — in jurisprudential context means an obligatory duty incumbent upon the subject

ai.seo_question: Is making a will (wasiyya) obligatory in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms through a chain of reliable narrators that making a bequest (wasiyya) is an established right and obligation incumbent upon every Muslim. This hadith aligns with the Quranic injunction in Surah al-Baqarah (2:180) commanding the making of a will before death. The questioner, Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, was a well-known jurisprudential inquirer of Imam al-Sadiq, and this terse yet authoritative response reflects the Imam's characteristic style of issuing binding legal guidance.
